title: Von der Leyen Visits Nuuk, Unveils €200M EU-Greenland Partnership Package, Proposes Doubling Aid to €530M
detail: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen concluded a two-day visit to Greenland on September 7, 2026 by announcing a €200 million ($232 million) 'EU-Greenland Partnership Package' in Nuuk, alongside a joint statement signed with Greenlandic and Danish officials. Von der Leyen also proposed doubling direct EU aid to Greenland to €530 million ($616 million) under the bloc's 2028–2034 budget period, with funds earmarked for infrastructure, clean energy, critical raw-materials exploration and potential AI data centers. Telling reporters in Nuuk that 'Greenland's future is for the people of Greenland and Denmark to decide. No one else,' von der Leyen framed the package as a direct counter to President Trump's continued annexation rhetoric; Greenland's Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen thanked the EU, saying 'through these challenging times, your support to us is unfailing... Greenland needs the European Union, and the European Union needs Greenland.' The visit's timing coincided with the opening days of NATO's Arctic Shield 2026 exercise and followed Trump's earlier threats of tariffs on Denmark and seven other allies after eight European nations deployed troops to Greenland in a January 2026 show of solidarity.

media.caption: EU Commission President von der Leyen announces a €200 million Greenland partnership package in Nuuk, September 7, 2026
